thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — high tail latency detected on continuous-batching path (p99 spike). Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall. Paging oncall: @Maya :rotating_light:

Maya: seeing p95 jump ~2s and p99 > 6s on cont-batch nodes in us-west-2. Streaming stalls flagged in traces. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/contbatch/latency?orgId=1 :eyes:

Aj: thanks, grabbing it. any customer 5xxs?

Maya: errors flat, no 5xx. Affected traffic is streaming/longer seq models — tail latency mainly. Traffic % small (~3%) but affects realtime customers.

Liam: linking playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/contbatch-tail. First mitigation: reduce max_batch_size for streaming route, decrease queue_wait_ms.

Sara: on prod right now: cont-batcher pods showing high queue depth and some long lived KV cache hold-ups. Kernel-level metrics show bursts of GPU CPU scheduling.

Maya: i'm going to flip a temporary routing rule to divert new streaming sessions to streaming-only fleet (lower latency) — will keep cont-batch for batch clients.

Aj: +1. Add a canary: divert 20% first. Use ops-bot to create route.

ops-bot: runbook command queued: ``/route update --name streaming-path --split 80:20 --dest streaming-fleet,contbatch-fleet --comment "live mitigation 6880012345"``

ops-bot: route update accepted. Rolling out 20% traffic to streaming-fleet.

Maya: metrics after 2m: p95 down 300ms, p99 down 1.8s for diverted traffic. cont-batch p99 still elevated for remaining 80%.

Ron: logs show contention on batch_scheduler when mixed-seqlen packing hits high variance. There's a hot-path where long sequences block packers because pack window waits for small sequences to fill, causing tail amplification.

Aj: can we temporarily enable pack-shed to prioritize short requests? There's an emergency flag in config: `batcher.pack_policy=prefer_short` and `batcher.shed_threshold=0.8`.

Maya: prepping a change. Pushing small config tweak via k8s configmap rollout: ``kubectl -n inference set configmap batcher-config --from-literal=pack_policy=prefer_short --from-literal=shed_threshold=0.8`` then restart deployment `cont-batcher` with zero-downtime rolling restart.

Sara: be careful, pack_policy affects accuracy profiles for some customers. Tagging customer-impacted list.

Maya: rolling change initiated.

Aj: meanwhile, create a short-lived autoscale to add 3 cont-batcher pods: ``scaler scale cont-batcher --replicas +3 --reason "emergency tail relief"``

ops-bot: scaler request accepted, scaling to +3.

Maya: after pack_policy + autoscale: cont-batch p95 improved 600ms, p99 dropped 2.4s (still above SLO of 1.5s). Streaming-fleet remains healthy.

Liam: need deeper root cause — suspects scheduling fairness issue: long seqs hold slot longer and preempt others. Can we get traces correlating sequence length to queue wait time? Prometheus query I use: ``histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(contbatch_queue_wait_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, seq_len_bucket))``

Ron: collected traces for three bad requests, attaching excerpt:```
span cont-batcher enqueue  t=0.000s
span packer wait        t=1.7s
span gpu-sched wait     t=3.2s
span kvcache lock       t=0.9s
```

Sara: kvcache ejection rate spiked at same time. Possible memory pressure causing eviction thrash and additional I/O.

Aj: can we temporarily increase kvcache capacity on affected nodes? There's a node-label flow: ``kubectl patch daemonset kvcache --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kvcache","env":[{"name":"KV_MAX_MEM","value":"6g"}]}]}}}}'``

Maya: patching KV_MAX_MEM to 6g on us-west-2 cont nodes.

Maya: after kvcache bump: eviction rate normalized, p99 down further to ~1.9s. Still above SLO though.

Liam: plan for next hour: 1) continue routing 20% to streaming-fleet 2) keep pack_policy prefer_short 3) monitor kvcache 4) run targeted rollback for any customers showing inference quality drift 5) run postmortem if not resolved in 4h.

Ron: investigating scheduler code path: we may need fairness token buckets updated — current implementation estimates cost by tokens=seq_len/64, but long seqs sometimes under-estimated because of early truncation. I can push a hotfix to use `tokens = max(tokens, gpu_duration_estimate(seq_len))` but need approval for patch.

Aj: approve hotfix if it's a non-invasive change. Timeboxed deploy to canary first.

Maya: handoff: i'm going offline in 30m. Handoff to @Liam — details: mitigations applied (route split 80/20, pack_policy, shed_threshold=0.8, kvcache mem +3 nodes), current p99 ~1.9s, customer impact: small set of realtime customers degraded but no 5xx. Ticket created: INC-6873, notifying account teams and CS.

Liam: taking over. I'll watch the dashboards and coordinate with Ron on the scheduler patch. If p99 < 1.5s within 60m, we'll start rolling back route split gradually.

ops-bot: incident update recorded: INC-6873 — mitigation actions logged.

Maya: quick note for postmortem: collect batching histograms, seq length distribution, pack fill times, kvcache evictions. Also export a sample of affected request IDs for replay.

Liam: On it. Assigning action items: Ron -> scheduler token fix PR and canary; Sara -> kvcache telemetry + correlate disk I/O; Aj -> customer comms and SLAs; Maya -> postmortem draft.

Ron: starting PR branch `fix/fairtokens-av1` and will post link.

Aj: pinging CS: "We’re seeing elevated tail latency for a small subset of streaming customers; mitigation applied; engineers are actively working; no request failures expected."

Maya: thanks team. I'll check in after my handoff window. Please escalate if p99 rises or any 5xx appear. :thumbsup:

Liam: logging final for now, will update thread with PR links and rollback plan.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 6880012345 status: mitigated->partial, oncall_handoff recorded -> Liam.

Liam: (later) PR: https://redwood.internal/pull/9876 — canary deployed, awaiting 15m of telemetry.

ops-bot: Canary metrics: cont-batch-canary p99 reduced 35% vs baseline. Proceeding with staged rollout per runbook.

Liam: rolling to 50% while watching. Will keep CS updated and close incident once p99 stable under SLO for 2 consecutive 10m windows.

Maya: nice work.
